subject: Aligning MAP and legal milestones for Meditech PO: sequencing MSA/DPA/order form
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@meditech.com>, Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + sequencing proposal for legal/procurement milestones

Laura — thanks again for the time today. As discussed, attaching an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP_v2.xlsx) that maps evaluation checkpoints to procurement/legal milestones so we can converge on a single close timeline. High-level asks in this email: 

- Can you confirm Meditech's preferred signature order (MSA first vs. order form first)? You mentioned procurement prefers a PO to trigger billing, but legal wanted DPA reviewed early.
- Please flag any internal review windows (security, legal, purchasing) and an approximate SLA for redlines (e.g., 5 business days).
- If you can share the PO template / billing contact, we'll draft the order form to match procurement fields.

Summary of proposed sequencing (in MAP_v2 tab "sequence"): 
1) Exchange commercial term sheet (done)
2) Redwood to submit redlined MSA + DPA (we attached redwood_msa_dpa_v3.pdf) — target 8/12
3) Meditech legal reviews; procurement prepares PO template in parallel — target 8/19
4) Order form finalized and signed after MSA baseline agreed — target 8/24
5) Technical kickoff and pilot start — target 9/1

I've set conservative targets to allow for a 1-pass redline + 1-pass procurement changes. If you prefer a different order (e.g., sign order form and then MSA with conditions), we can update the MAP.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx, redwood_msa_dpa_v3.pdf, orderform-draft.docx (order form is a skeleton — will populate with PO fields once you share).

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@meditech.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + sequencing proposal for legal/procurement milestones

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement prefers to get an approved PO before billing; however, Legal has requested the DPA reviewed early because of data residency clauses. We usually do a contract signature (MSA) and PO in parallel, but in cases with DPA negotiation we ask vendors to accept an interim SOW/order form pending final DPA.
- Typical review SLA: Legal 7–10 business days for an initial redline (may be faster if it's a one-off change). Procurement: usually 3–5 business days to issue a PO once terms are agreed.
- I'll attach the PO template (separately) and introduce you to our billing contact — putting John Mills on this thread.

Proposed tweak: Can we split the MAP sequence into two parallel tracks — (A) Legal/DPA negotiation and (B) Commercial/order form finalization — with a convergence point where the PO is cut contingent on MSA baseline and DPA checklist items? That would let procurement start internal approvals while legal finishes technical clauses.

I'll review your MSA/DPA PDF and come back with redline expectations by 8/13.

—Laura

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + sequencing proposal for legal/procurement milestones

Laura — perfect, thanks. Splitting into two parallel tracks makes sense and aligns with how we've closed other regulated customers. Updated plan below (also reflected in MAP_v2.xlsx):

Track A — Legal/DPA (owner: Meditech legal + Redwood legal)
- 8/12: Redwood submits baseline MSA+DPA (done)
- 8/13–8/20: Meditech legal review (7 business days target)
- If redlines are extensive, consider a 1:1 legal sync call mid-review (we can facilitate).

Track B — Commercial / Procurement (owner: Meditech procurement + Redwood sales/finance)
- 8/12–8/17: Procurement prepares PO template and internal approvals
- 8/18: Redwood finalizes order form with PO fields and sample SOW
- 8/19–8/24: Procurement issues PO contingent on MSA baseline and DPA checklist
Convergence: Target 8/24 for both tracks to reach production sign-off; pilot provisioning 9/1.
Action items: 
- Laura: please share PO template and billing contact (John — assigning to you)
- Vanessa: can you prepare a short DPA checklist (3–5 items) that procurement can use to decide whether to issue a PO contingent vs. final?
- Marcus: draft an order form populated with our default billing flow once we have the template — assign to 'orderform-draft.docx'.

Thanks — I'll update the MAP and push a fresh copy to the Drive link.

Cheers,
Priyom

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: DPA checklist + gating language for procurement (Meditech)

Team — quick internal note after Laura's last message. Draft DPA checklist below to keep procurement comfortable with issuing a contingent PO: 

1) Data residency confirmation: customer data stored in US regions only (ok to confirm on our side).
2) Subprocessor list + right to notice (we'll provide current list; changes require 30-day notice).
3) Standard security controls: SOC2 Type II attestation available; provide copy of SOC2 report under NDA.
4) Incident notification SLA: 72 hours initial notification; full report within 30 days.
5) Minimum retention/deletion commitments per customer request (we support configurable retention).

Procurement gating language suggestion for PO: "PO issuance is contingent on agreement of MSA baseline and confirmation of DPA checklist items 1–5; final PO and billing will be issued upon resolution of any material DPA redlines."

I've uploaded Vanessa_DPA_checklist_v1.docx to the shared Drive (link in hubspot note). Sending to Priyom to attach to MAP before we share with procurement.
